pages.text: "Soup tastes best when it's boiling hot!" Leo the know-it-all fox sat at the middle of the long table. Steam rose from a pot on the stove. "I know everything. It tastes bad when it's cold."

Grandma Bear, who ran the lodge, stood by the pot with a ladle. An empty bowl waited at each seat. Rudi the hungry squirrel waited with both hands on their lap. Rudi whispered to Leo, "We start when Grandma sits down."
Leo pretended not to hear and tore bread from the basket. "I always eat bread first." Crumbs scattered over the table.
Grandma sat and lifted her spoon. The ladle passed from her hand to Rudi's. Busy chewing bread, Leo couldn't hold out his bowl.
The ladle went around and returned to Grandma. She scraped the pot bottom and poured a little into Leo's bowl. The soup was lukewarm, without a bit of steam.
Steam rose from Rudi's bowl. Leo stirred his soup with a spoon. Still lukewarm. He rested his muzzle on the table and said nothing.
Hanging the ladle on the pot, Grandma asked, "Leo, where did the ladle start?" "At your seat," he said softly. "Yes. Grandma lifts her spoon—start!"
At lunch the next day, Leo waited without touching the bread basket. Grandma sat and raised her spoon. Leo held both hands neatly together. "Start!"

When his turn came, Leo quickly held out his empty bowl. It filled with steaming hot soup. "One, everyone sits together! Two, Grandma lifts her spoon! Three, then start!" Leo raised his muzzle, blew gently, and ate a spoonful.
Grandma wrapped an arm around Leo's shoulders and patted his back. Wait to eat, and it reaches your bowl at its hottest. "Grandma lifts her spoon—start!" Leo held his spoon high.
